lines.japanese: 「羽田君ってゲーム得意なんだよね」
lines.english: “You're good at video games, aren't you, Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「え、前にも言ったじゃない。そんなに得意なわけじゃないし、普通だよ」
lines.english: “What? I told you before, I’m not especially good. I’m just average.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんと一緒に出かけるのは嬉しい。
lines.english: I was happy simply to be going somewhere with Watarai.

lines.japanese: さらに場所がゲームショップっていうのもよかった。僕が何度も訪れている場所、言ってみればホームグラウンドだ。
lines.english: That our destination was a game store made it better still. I had been there many times. You could call it my home turf.

lines.japanese: だけど一年生のときに森里君から「あんまりおまえの場合、みんなの前でゲームの話しない方がいいよ」と言われてから、クラスのひととはこの手の話をできるだけ控えてるんだ。
lines.english: But in our first year, Morisato had told me, “In your case, you probably shouldn't talk about games too much in front of everyone.” Ever since, I had avoided the subject with my classmates whenever possible.

lines.japanese: おととい話したときは案の定うわついて、渡来さんが少し引いてた。今日はぼろを出さないようにしたい。
lines.english: Sure enough, I had gotten carried away when we talked two days ago, and Watarai had recoiled a little. Today I wanted to avoid giving myself away.

lines.japanese: かと言ってゲームショップへ行くのに、ゲームの話をまるでしないわけにもいかない。
lines.english: Then again, we could hardly go to a game store without talking about games at all.

lines.japanese: こういうときは自分の話じゃなくて相手に主導権を委ねるのがいい。とネットで見た気がする。僕は渡来さんに話を預けることにした。
lines.english: At times like these, it was better to hand the other person the conversational reins instead of talking about yourself. I thought I had read that online. I decided to leave the conversation to Watarai.

lines.japanese: 「あ、えっと……渡来さんはどんなゲームが好きなのかな」
lines.english: “Um... what sort of games do you like, Watarai?”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　ゲーム？」
lines.english: “Hm? Games?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、買いに行くんでしょ。傾向くらいは聞いといた方がいいかなって」
lines.english: “Yes. We’re going to buy one, aren’t we? I thought I should at least know what sort you like.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうだよね。んー、でも私、弟的な子が持ってたやつしか知らないんだよね」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Hmm. But the only one I know is the thing this boy who’s sort of like a little brother had.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それでいいよ。教えて」
lines.english: “That's fine. Tell me about it.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、じゃあ――こう、四角くて色は白で……ああ、あと、ぴこぴこするのが二つついてるの」
lines.english: “All right, then—it was square and white... Oh, and it had two little beep-boop things attached.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、もしかして真ん中にガチャッて差しこむやつかな」
lines.english: “Oh, could it be the kind where you slot something into the middle with a clunk?”

lines.japanese: 「そう、それそれ！　さすが羽田君、詳しいね」
lines.english: “Yes, that’s it! I knew you’d know, Haneda. You really are an expert.”

lines.japanese: それはソフトじゃなくてハードだ。
lines.english: That was the hardware, not the software.

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは好きな音楽を聞かれたら、コンポやプレーヤーの種類を答えるんだろうか。
lines.english: If someone asked Watarai what music she liked, would she name a kind of stereo or music player?

lines.japanese: 「なるほど……うん、なんとなく分かったよ」
lines.english: “I see... Yes, I think I’ve got it.”

lines.japanese: 「わっ、ほんとに？」
lines.english: “Wow, really?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんがゲームをやったことないってことがね。
lines.english: I had gathered that Watarai had never played a video game.

lines.japanese: でも好みの傾向は聞いておかないといけない。
lines.english: But I still needed some idea of her tastes.

lines.japanese: 「えっと、それじゃあ……そっちのガチャッと差し込む方の話を聞いてもいいかな」
lines.english: “Then... could you tell me about the thing that slots in with a clunk?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いいよ。なんでも聞いて」
lines.english: “Of course. Ask me anything.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、ガチャッとするやつはどんなのが好きなの？」
lines.english: “Then what kind of thing that went clunk did you like?”

lines.japanese: 「好きっていうか、なんかプラスチックのやつ。紫がかった四角いのしか知らない」
lines.english: “I wouldn’t say I liked one in particular. It was some plastic thing. I only know the purplish square kind.”

lines.japanese: それはＲＯＭカセットだ。渡来さんは好きな音楽のジャンルを聞かれたら、メディアを答えるんだろうか。
lines.english: She meant a ROM cartridge. If someone asked Watarai what genre of music she liked, would she answer with the storage medium?

lines.japanese: 渡来さんと僕の差は開く一方だ。
lines.english: The gulf between Watarai and me only widened.

lines.japanese: 「わー、いっぱいあるね」
lines.english: “Wow, there are so many.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはゲームショップに初めて入ったみたいだ。
lines.english: Watarai looked as though she had never set foot in a game store before.

lines.japanese: 多分どの棚を探せばいいのかも分からないだろう。ただでさえ最近は、家庭用から携帯型までハードも多くて、さらにそのソフトを各ジャンルに分けると、棚がいくつあっても足りないくらいなんだ。
lines.english: She probably had no idea which shelves to search. These days there were already so many platforms, from home consoles to handhelds, and once you divided all their software by genre, you could never have enough shelves.

lines.japanese: さて、この中からジャンルさえよく分かってない渡来さんのお目当てを探しだすのは骨の折れる作業だぞ……。
lines.english: Finding the game Watarai wanted somewhere in all this, when she did not even understand the genres, was going to be quite a job...

lines.japanese: 「ねえねえ、羽田君」
lines.english: “Hey, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。どしたの渡来さん」
lines.english: “Yes? What is it, Watarai?”

lines.japanese: 「シュミレーションゲームってなに？」
lines.english: “What’s a ‘similation game’?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、シミュレーションゲーム。それは……」
lines.english: “Oh, a simulation game. That’s...”

lines.japanese: うーんでも、森里君に言われてるし、あんまり知ったかぶりはしない方がいいな。
lines.english: But Morisato had warned me. Better not parade my knowledge too much.

lines.japanese: 「さあ、よく分からないよ」
lines.english: “I don't really know.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん、そうなんだあ」
lines.english: “Oh. I see.”

lines.japanese: うーん、ほんとはそんなの簡単に説明できるんだけど。日本史で言えば大化の改新とか大塩平八郎の乱くらい当たり前のことだ。
lines.english: But it would have been so easy to explain. It was as elementary as the Taika Reform or Oshio Heihachiro’s rebellion in Japanese history.

lines.japanese: 「ねえねえ、羽田君」
lines.english: “Hey, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。今度はどしたの渡来さん」
lines.english: “Yes? What is it this time, Watarai?”

lines.japanese: 「これどんなゲーム？」
lines.english: “What sort of game is this?”

lines.japanese: そう言って渡来さんは棚から一つソフトを手に取った。その箱には『シャッフル！　オンザステージ』と書いてある。
lines.english: With that, Watarai took a game from the shelf. The box read *SHUFFLE! ON THE STAGE*.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、それは……」
lines.english: “Oh, that's...”

lines.japanese: 僕がいま注目してて、一番やりたいゲームなんだ。
lines.english: The game at the very top of my wish list. The one I wanted to play most of all.

lines.japanese: 神にも悪魔にも凡人にもなれる男、主人公・土見稟が５（＋２）人のヒロインに振りまわされる大人気のアドベンチャーゲーム。
lines.english: A wildly popular adventure game in which its hero, Rin Tsuchimi—a man who can become a god, a demon, or an ordinary mortal—is buffeted about by five (plus two) heroines.

lines.japanese: 開門と呼ばれる事象によって神界と魔界が人間界と繋がった、ていう世界観でね。メインヒロインのうちふたりは、それぞれの世界のお姫様たちなんだ。
lines.english: Its world was one where an event called the Opening had connected the Realm of the Gods and the Realm of the Demons to the human world. Two of the main heroines were princesses from those respective realms.

lines.japanese: ある日彼女たちが両隣りに引っ越してくることで始まる、ドタバタ恋愛コメディ。人気キャラは意見が分かれるところだけど、僕個人の好みで言うとまあ、幼馴染みの――
lines.english: The slapstick romantic comedy began when they moved into the houses on either side of his. People disagreed over the most popular girl, but if you asked me, it had to be the childhood friend—

lines.japanese: 「さあ、よく分からないよ」
lines.english: “I don't really know.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん、そうなんだあ」
lines.english: “Oh. I see.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、このひと耳尖ってるのなんでだろ。えーと、リシア、ソサス……？」
lines.english: “Oh, why does this girl have pointed ears? Let’s see... Lisia... Sosas...?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、それは……」
lines.english: “Oh, that's...”

lines.japanese: リシアンサスは神界のお姫様でね、その世界の住人はみんな、いわゆるエルフ耳なんだ。こっちのネリネ、彼女は魔界のお姫様で、ほら、もっと耳が尖ってるでしょ？
lines.english: Lisianthus is a princess of the Realm of the Gods. Everyone there has what you might call elf ears. And this is Nerine. She’s a princess of the Realm of the Demons, and look—her ears are even pointier, see?

lines.japanese: ちなみにシアは、彼女の出生にまつわる重大な秘密を隠しもっていてね。なんと彼女の中には……おっと、これ以上はネタバレになるから言わない方がいいかな。
lines.english: Incidentally, Sia is hiding an enormous secret about her birth. In fact, inside her there is... No. That would be a spoiler. Better not say any more.

lines.japanese: まあリシアンサスも素直で明るくて可愛いキャラなんだけど、僕個人の好みでいうと一番は幼馴染――
lines.english: Lisianthus is straightforward and cheerful and adorable too, but if you ask me, my favorite is still the childhood friend—

lines.japanese: 「さあ、よく分からないよ」
lines.english: “I don't really know.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん、そうなんだあ」
lines.english: “Oh. I see.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは箱を棚へ戻しながら、その横のパッケージを手に取った。
lines.english: Watarai put the box back on the shelf and picked up the package beside it.

lines.japanese: 「このソウルリン――」
lines.english: “And this Soul Lin—”

lines.japanese: 「さあ、よく分からないよ」
lines.english: “I don't really know.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん、じゃあこの――」
lines.english: “Oh. Then what about—”

lines.japanese: 「さあ、よく分からないな」
lines.english: “I don’t really know that one either.”

lines.japanese: 僕は思ったよりゲームに詳しくないことになった。
lines.english: I had succeeded in making myself seem surprisingly ignorant about games.

lines.japanese: 「うーん、見つからないなー」
lines.english: “Hmm. I can't find it.”

lines.japanese: 「渡来さん、そろそろいいじゃない。なんのゲームを探してるか教えてよ」
lines.english: “Watarai, isn’t it about time you told me which game you’re looking for?”

lines.japanese: 探しはじめてから１０分ほどが経過した。渡来さんはどうも一人で探したいみたいで、僕はタイトルも教えられていなかった。
lines.english: We had been searching for about ten minutes. Watarai apparently wanted to find it herself, and had not even told me the title.

lines.japanese: 「んー、やっぱひとりじゃ無理かあ……」
lines.english: “Hmm. I suppose I can't do it alone after all...”

lines.japanese: 「なんだっけ、ＲＰＧゲーム？　ってどれかな？」
lines.english: “What was it again? An RPG game? Where would those be?”

lines.japanese: 「違うよ渡来さん。ロールプレイングゲーム。略してＲＰＧだから、それだとＲＰＧＧになっちゃうよ」
lines.english: “No, Watarai. Role-playing game. RPG is already short for that, so what you said would make it RPGG.”

lines.japanese: 「うーんと、だからそのＲＰＧＧゲーム？　はどこにあるのかな」
lines.english: “Hmm. So where are the RPGG games?”

lines.japanese: 「ロールプレイングゲームだけど、ＲＰＧならこの辺かな。品揃えがいいから、色んなゲームがあると思うよ。例えばこの『オクラマカンサーガ』っていうのはね」
lines.english: “They’re role-playing games. The RPG section should be around here. This store has a good selection, so there should be all kinds. Take this Okuramakan Saga, for instance—”

lines.japanese: 「ありがと。じゃあ、ここから探してみるね」
lines.english: “Thank you. I'll try looking through these.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。分からないことがあれば声をかけて」
lines.english: “All right. Call me if there's anything you don't understand.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんがゲームを選びはじめたので、僕は邪魔をしないことにした。人が選ぶときは話しかけない方がいいと思うんだ。僕はその裏側にある、最新中古コーナーに体を向けた。
lines.english: Watarai began choosing a game, so I decided not to interfere. It was best not to talk to people while they were deciding. I turned toward the recent used releases on the other side of the shelf.

lines.japanese: あっ『ささやきマテリアル』のドラマシリーズ第一弾じゃないか。懐かしいなあ。一晩くらいかけてやったんだよなあ。
lines.english: Oh, wasn't that the first drama installment of *Whisper Material*? How nostalgic. I had spent nearly an entire night playing it.

lines.japanese: そうだ『ささやきマテリアル』の本編って、いまはどのくらいの値段なのかな。うわっ、３００円で買えるんだ。穂乃香シナリオなんて、今やっても面白いのに。
lines.english: Oh, right—what was the main *Whisper Material* game going for these days? Whoa, three hundred yen? Honoka’s route would still be good today.

lines.japanese: あれ、これって――
lines.english: Wait. Was this—
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: ──振りむくと渡来さんの動きが止まっていた。
lines.english: —I turned around and saw that Watarai had frozen in place.

lines.japanese: 僕の視線に気づいたのか、渡来さんの頭もこっちへ向いた。
lines.english: Perhaps she noticed me looking, because she turned her head my way.

lines.japanese: 「え？　なに、見つけたの？」
lines.english: “What is it? Did you find it?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、なんとなくこれかなって……じゃ、買ってくるね」
lines.english: “Yes. I have a feeling this is it... I’ll go buy it, then.”

lines.japanese: 「それじゃあおれも付いていこうか？　店長さんがすごくいいひとだから挨拶したいんだ」
lines.english: “Want me to come with you? The manager’s a great guy, and I’d like to say hello.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ、じゃあ店長さんと話してて」
lines.english: “Oh, really? Then you can talk to the manager.”

lines.japanese: 「え、渡来さんも一緒にどう？　店長さんも喜ぶと思うな。女の子とかお年寄りとか外人さんとか、とにかく珍しいお客さんと話をするのが好きなひとなんだ。ほら、渡来さん、なんか特別な顔してるし」
lines.english: “Why don’t you come too? I think he’d be pleased. He loves talking to unusual customers—girls, old people, foreigners, anyone out of the ordinary. And, well, you have a special sort of face.”

lines.japanese: 「なに、特別な顔って。私の顔って危険物指定でもされてるの」
lines.english: “What’s that supposed to mean, a special face? Has mine been officially designated hazardous material?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　だって渡来さん、特別綺麗な顔してるじゃん」
lines.english: “What? I only mean you have an exceptionally beautiful face.”

lines.japanese: 「は、羽田君はときどき、とんでもなくハートをついてくるなあ……」
lines.english: “H-Haneda, sometimes you hit a girl right in the heart out of nowhere...”

lines.japanese: 「分かった、じゃあ羽田君も顔馴染みみたいだし、ちょっとだけなら」
lines.english: “All right. Since you seem to know him, I suppose I can spare a minute.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そうだね……あっ」
lines.english: “Yes, that's—oh.”

lines.japanese: そうだ、いつもの調子で店長さんと話したら、僕がゲームに詳しいってことがバレてしまう。
lines.english: That was right. If I talked to the manager the way I usually did, Watarai would find out how much I knew about games.

lines.japanese: 「あっ、えっと、ごめん。おれから言いだして悪いんだけど、やっぱりちょっとトイレに行ってきていいかな」
lines.english: “Oh, um, sorry. I know I was the one who suggested it, but would you mind if I went to the restroom after all?”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ。うんじゃあ、ささっと買ってくるよ」
lines.english: “Oh, all right. Then I’ll hurry up and buy it.”

lines.japanese: 僕らは店の外で再集合の約束をして別れた。
lines.english: We agreed to meet outside the store and went our separate ways.

lines.japanese: 「あー、よかった、見つかった。羽田君、今日はありがとね」
lines.english: “Ah, good. I found it. Thanks for today, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 小さな袋を鞄の中にしまう渡来さんと一緒に店を出た。
lines.english: I left the store with Watarai as she tucked the small bag into her schoolbag.

lines.japanese: 「いや、いいよ。それでなにを買ったの？」
lines.english: “It was nothing. So what did you buy?”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　今はナイショ。クリアしたら教えてあげるね」
lines.english: “Hm? It's a secret for now. I'll tell you once I've beaten it.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そうだね。時間がかかるかもしれないけど、待ってるよ」
lines.english: “All right. It might take a while, but I’ll wait.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんがどんなゲームを買ったのかは興味がある。たぶん彼女ひとりじゃクリアは難しいだろうし、行きづまったら手伝ってあげよう。
lines.english: I was curious what sort of game Watarai had bought. It would probably be hard for her to finish alone, so if she got stuck, I would help.

lines.japanese: 「それで、羽田君の買いたいやつは？」
lines.english: “And what about the game you wanted to buy?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんが僕の鞄の中を覗きこもうとする。
lines.english: Watarai tried to peer into my schoolbag.

lines.japanese: 「あ、いいんだ。おれはまた今度来たときに買うから」
lines.english: “Oh, never mind. I’ll buy it next time I come.”

lines.japanese: 「でも鞄から私のと同じ袋が見えるよ？」
lines.english: “But I can see a bag just like mine inside yours.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、これは違うんだ。だから気にしないで」
lines.english: “No, that's something else. Don't worry about it.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん。まあ羽田君ってあんまりゲーム詳しくないもんね。私が見ても分からないよね」
lines.english: “Hmm. Well, you don’t know that much about games, do you? I probably wouldn’t understand it even if I saw it.”

lines.japanese: 「うんそうなんだ。まあ、普通かな」
lines.english: “Right. Exactly. I’m about average.”

lines.japanese: 僕は『シャッフル！　オンザステージ』が入った袋を鞄のいちばん奥へ押しこんだ。
lines.english: I pushed the bag containing *SHUFFLE! ON THE STAGE* into the very bottom of my schoolbag.
